# TypeScript rules

Apply these rules to every TypeScript file you write or review. React rules are in `react-rules`, Next.js rules in `nextjs-rules`. The first section is always in force; open a rule from the table when the task touches it.

## Always apply (critical, high)

### Type a value of unknown shape as unknown and narrow it, never as any

_high · typescript_

**Rule.** Type data whose shape is not known yet (parsed JSON, a caught error, a third-party payload) as `unknown` and narrow it with a type guard or a schema parse before using it. Never write `any`, neither as an annotation nor as `as any`.

**Why.** `any` turns off checking for the value and everything derived from it, so a missing field or a wrong type compiles and fails only at runtime; `unknown` makes the compiler reject every use until the code has checked the shape.

**Correct:**

```ts
function readTitle(payload: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof payload === "object" && payload !== null && "title" in payload && typeof payload.title === "string") {
    return payload.title.trim();
  }
  return null;
}
```

| medium | [Import from another folder through the ~/ path alias, not a deep relative path](references/rules.md#import-from-another-folder-through-the--path-alias-not-a-deep-relative-path) — ../../.. paths break when a file moves and hide where the import comes from; ~/ is rooted at src. | typescript |
| medium | [Model a closed set of strings as an as const object plus a same-named type](references/rules.md#model-a-closed-set-of-strings-as-an-as-const-object-plus-a-same-named-type) — Never a TypeScript enum or a hand-written literal union; one const object is both the value and the type. | typescript |
| medium | [Refer to a closed-set value through its const object, never as a raw string literal](references/rules.md#refer-to-a-closed-set-value-through-its-const-object-never-as-a-raw-string-literal) — A raw literal in an Extract silently becomes never when a value is renamed; OrderStatus.PAID fails to compile instead. | typescript |
| medium | [Write array types as Array<T>, never T[]](references/rules.md#write-array-types-as-arrayt-never-t) — T[] binds tighter than \|, so string \| number[] means a string or an array of numbers, not an array of either. | typescript |
| low | [Keep tutorials, how-to guides, reference and explanation on separate pages](references/rules.md#keep-tutorials-how-to-guides-reference-and-explanation-on-separate-pages) — The Diátaxis split: each page serves one reader need, so none mixes lessons, recipes, facts and background. | any |
| low | [Record every public change in CHANGELOG.md in the Keep a Changelog format](references/rules.md#record-every-public-change-in-changelogmd-in-the-keep-a-changelog-format) — Each pull request that changes public behaviour adds an entry under Unreleased, grouped by kind. | any |
| low | [Comment only a reason the code cannot show](references/rules.md#comment-only-a-reason-the-code-cannot-show) — Default to no comment; write one only for a hidden constraint, a subtle invariant or a workaround. | typescript |
| low | [Write every warranted comment as a JSDoc block, not a // line](references/rules.md#write-every-warranted-comment-as-a-jsdoc-block-not-a--line) — A /** */ comment above a function, type or statement shows in editor hovers; a // comment shows nowhere else. | typescript |
| low | [Declare every named function with the function keyword](references/rules.md#declare-every-named-function-with-the-function-keyword) — A const arrow is not hoisted and throws if called before its line has run; a declaration is hoisted. | typescript |
| low | [Write a callback argument as an inline arrow function](references/rules.md#write-a-callback-argument-as-an-inline-arrow-function) — Arrow functions belong only where a callback is passed; there they keep the outer this and stay short. | typescript |
